upstream.time_semantics: Madeira timeline date is UTC; the official page says the radar reference time is UTC and limits display history to the latest three hours.

grid.derivation: The official mapbuilder passes these exact bounds to Leaflet ImageOverlay for each Madeira timeline path; pixel centers are derived from the image dimensions.

upstream.value_semantics: ordinal rainfall-intensity legend intervals, stored as categories with unit 1

differences: The legacy luminance-to-0..224 transform is rejected as a physical-value decoder. Pixels are mapped to ordinal rainfall-intensity intervals using the official legend's color strip and printed labels.
The adapter does not interpolate point rainfall rates from color position; numeric mm/h values are not present in the resulting field.
Transparent pixels are category 0 with below-detection quality, not a claim of zero rain. Opaque black pixels are missing because black is not part of the official legend.
The native image is a rectangular geographic overlay; no circular radar-range mask is inferred from the display.

The image/legend relationship is established by the public Madeira page's legend and map script, which applies the same bounds to every Madeira timeline path. The retained fixture's used colors fall within 9.5 RGB levels of the legend ramp.
evidence: live exact-path reacquisition on 2026-09-21; bytes and SHA-256 matched the retained fixture
scientific_limits: Values are ordinal legend intervals, not continuous rainfall-rate estimates; the provider's display legend alone does not establish the numeric value represented by every source RGB value.
Transparent pixels cannot distinguish true no-rain from below-threshold or unobserved regions.
IPMA describes the map as informational; it must not be treated as an official incident/accident record.
